input:
We are porting an ISP tuning library from MT6989 to QCS8550. The identical ISP pipeline configuration produces 18% lower throughput on QCS8550 despite the QCS8550 having a higher nominal clock. After ingesting both SoC IP-XACT register maps, the knowledge graph shows a register-level difference. Relevant graph query output:

  MT6989  ISP_RDMA_CTRL @ 0x15220010: field BURST_LEN[7:4] default=0xF (16-beat burst)
  QCS8550 ISP_RDMA_CTRL @ 0x0A810010: field BURST_LEN[7:4] default=0x4 (4-beat burst)

  MT6989  ISP_WB_GAIN   @ 0x15220100: field FRAC_BITS[3:2]  = 0b10 (12.4 fixed-point)
  QCS8550 ISP_WB_GAIN   @ 0x0A810100: field FRAC_BITS[3:2]  = 0b01 (12.2 fixed-point, less precision)

The QCS8550 ISP RDMA is defaulting to 4-beat bursts instead of 16-beat bursts, which would dramatically reduce DRAM read throughput for the ISP. Additionally, the white-balance gain precision differs, which may affect image quality. How do I safely override the QCS8550 BURST_LEN default to 0xF at driver init without breaking the existing RDMA arbitration, and what regression tests should cover the precision change in WB_GAIN?
